sec1.titulo: Arguing about what did not happen
abertura: You do this in Portuguese every week: say what would have been different if one fact had been another.
Mark the two things a hypothetical argument has to do to be worth making.

itens.t: It has to change something that is still open.
itens.porque: Yes. A hypothetical that changes nothing is a curiosity; the test is what it does to the decision in front of you.

itens.t: It has to prove the other side acted in bad faith.
itens.porque: No — and reaching for bad faith turns an argument about facts into an argument about people.

itens.t: It has to name the one fact that would have been different.
itens.porque: Yes. One fact, named. Two or three at once and nobody can follow which one you are arguing from.

itens.t: It has to be about the most serious point in the case.
itens.porque: No. It has to be about the point that is still open, which is often not the most serious one.

itens.t: It has to be impossible to disagree with.
itens.porque: No. If it were impossible to disagree with, there would be nothing to argue — the skill is holding it when someone does.

sec1.rationale: A hypothetical that changes nothing still open is an observation, not an argument -- and the person listening will say so.

nota.titulo: The question your interlocutor will ask
nota.texto:
What does the hypothetical buy us? is the objection you should expect, and it is a fair one. The answer is never “because it is true”. It is always what it changes about the decision in front of us.

That is why the form matters: if X had been…, we would not be… puts the consequence in the present, where the decision is.

nota.titulo: “Even if” is the one that does the work
nota.texto:
It lets you agree with something and lose nothing: Even if you are right about the timing, it would not change what the witness says today. The concession is real, and the argument survives it.

Refusing to concede anything is what makes an argument sound weak, not strong — and it is the habit hardest to break in a second language, because conceding requires a form you have to reach for.

sec3.titulo: Which fact would have to change
abertura: Six statements about the same case. Say what each one is doing.

doc.texto: The statement was not recorded on the night of the incident. It was taken eleven days later, after the witness had spoken to two other people present. The defence argues that the delay explains the inconsistencies; the prosecution argues that the inconsistencies are the point.

opcoes: arguing what would have been different
stating a fact from the summary

itens.t: "The statement was taken eleven days later."
itens.ok: stating a fact from the summary
itens.porque: A fact from the summary: quotable, and where the argument anchors.

itens.t: "If it had been taken that night, the inconsistencies would not be there."
itens.ok: arguing what would have been different
itens.porque: The hypothetical — what the missing condition would have produced.

itens.t: "Even if the delay explains some of it, it does not explain all of it."
itens.ok: conceding something
itens.porque: A concession, with the turn kept: grant part, hold the rest.

itens.t: "And what would that change now?"
itens.ok: asking what it changes
itens.porque: The question that follows a hypothetical, and the one you should expect. Answer it before it is asked.

itens.t: "She had spoken to two other people first."
itens.ok: stating a fact from the summary
itens.porque: Fact. It is what makes the third version explainable without accusing anyone.

itens.t: "Had she been asked that night, we would have one version, not three."
itens.ok: arguing what would have been different
itens.porque: The same hypothetical in the inverted form — more formal, and one syllable shorter to say.

nota.titulo: The two hypotheticals are built differently
nota.texto:
If it had been taken… and Had she been asked… say the same thing. The second drops the if and inverts — it is more formal, and it is what you will read in written argument in English.

You do not have to use it. You do have to recognise it when the other side does.

abertura: Mark the two that concede something and still hold the argument.

itens.t: "Even if that were true, it would not change the timeline."
itens.porque: Concede the premise, keep the conclusion. Nothing is given away.

itens.t: "You may be right about that. Let us leave it there."
itens.porque: The concession alone. It sounds gracious and ends the argument against you.

itens.t: "That is a fair point -- the difference is that the witness had already spoken to two people."
itens.porque: Concession, then the fact that changes what it means. This is the pair to practise.

itens.t: "I disagree with everything you have said."
itens.porque: No concession at all. It costs you the goodwill and it does not answer anything.

itens.t: "Fine, if you insist."
itens.porque: Surrender with irritation attached — the worst of both.

sec4.rationale: A concession that ends the sentence gives the point away. A concession followed by the difference is or it would not change keeps it.

nota.titulo: Where it goes wrong in a second language
nota.texto:
Conceding needs two moves in one breath: accept, then turn. In your own language you do it without noticing. In English the second move needs a form you have to reach for — and if it does not come, the sentence stops after the concession and sounds like surrender.

That is why this lesson practises the pair, never the concession alone.

abertura: Complete each one so that the consequence lands in the present, where the decision is.

itens.t: If the statement had been taken that night,
alts: we would not be arguing about it now
it would be better
the witness was more reliable
itens.ok: we would not be arguing about it now

itens.t: Even if the delay explains part of it,
alts: I accept your point entirely
that is what I have been saying
it does not explain the third version
itens.ok: it does not explain the third version

itens.t: Had she been asked before she spoke to the others,
alts: she would have been telling the truth
the delay would not exist
we would have one account instead of three
itens.ok: we would have one account instead of three

itens.t: That is a fair point --
alts: and I have nothing to add
the difference is that nothing was recorded
so we can move on
itens.ok: the difference is that nothing was recorded

nota.titulo: Look at what the wrong endings do
nota.texto:
They are all grammatical. What they lack is a consequence that touches the decision in front of you. It would be better is true and buys nothing; I accept your point entirely concedes and stops.

The test is the objection from activity 1: what does it buy us?

abertura: Complete the paragraph. Watch the verb forms -- there is no word bank here on purpose.
itens: If the statement {had been|150px} taken on the night, we {would not be|170px} discussing three versions now.
Even if the delay {explains|150px} part of it, it does not explain why the third account appeared.
Had she {been|110px} asked before she spoke to the others, we {would have|150px} one version.

nota.titulo: Why there is no word bank in this one
nota.texto:
In a vocabulary gap-fill the bank is required — without the candidates on screen, “complete the sentence” is not lexical recall, it is a memory test.

Here the gap asks for the FORM of the verb, and the bank would hand you the answer. This is the one exercise in the lesson that measures precision without conversational pressure — and it exists so that the lesson can tell the difference between not knowing the form and not reaching it in time.

itens.t: "The statement was taken eleven days later."
itens.ok: a fact from the summary
itens.porque: A fact. It is on the page, it is not in dispute, and it is where an argument starts — the hypothetical has to hang on something.

itens.t: "If it had been taken that night, we would have one version."
itens.ok: what would have been different
itens.porque: The hypothetical. Second conditional in the past: the condition did not happen, and you are naming what it would have produced.

itens.t: "Even if the delay explains some of it, it does not explain all."
itens.ok: a concession
itens.porque: A concession — and note the second half. Without it does not explain all, the sentence stops at the concession and reads as surrender.

itens.t: "She had already spoken to two other people."
itens.ok: a fact from the summary
itens.porque: Another fact, and the one that makes the hypothetical worth making.

itens.t: "Had she been asked that night, the third account would not exist."
itens.ok: what would have been different
itens.porque: Same move as the second item, in the inverted form: had she been instead of if she had been. More formal, same meaning.

itens.t: "That is a fair point -- the difference is nothing was recorded."
itens.ok: a concession
itens.porque: A concession with the turn attached. The difference is… is what keeps the point after granting it.

nota.titulo: Three moves, and you need all three in one turn
nota.texto: The fact anchors you, the hypothetical makes the argument, and the concession is what keeps the other side listening. An argument built only of the middle one sounds like speculation; one built only of the first sounds like a summary.

itens.t: "Even if that were true, it would not change the timeline."
itens.porque: Grants the premise and holds the conclusion. You lose nothing by conceding something that does not decide anything.

itens.t: "You may be right. Let us leave it there."
itens.porque: The concession with nothing after it. In writing it looks polite; out loud it ends the argument in the other person’s favour.

itens.t: "That is fair -- the difference is she had spoken to two people first."
itens.porque: Four words of concession, then the fact he does not have. That is the whole move.

itens.t: "Fine, if you insist."
itens.porque: Not a concession — a retreat with an edge on it. It concedes the point and the goodwill at the same time.

cn11d.rationale: Accept, then turn. A concession that ends the sentence gives the point away.

nota.titulo: The second move is the one that disappears
nota.texto: Under pressure, in a second language, the sentence often stops right after the concession — and what was meant as strength lands as surrender. Practise the pair, never the concession alone.

evenif.titulo: Saying what did not happen, and what it changes
abertura: Three moves. In a real turn you need all three, and usually in this order.

tabela:
The statement was taken eleven days later.
Anchors you. Nobody argues with it, and it is where the hypothetical stands.

IF it had been taken that night, we would not be arguing about it now.
The formal version drops the if and inverts: Had she been asked that night… You will read it more than you say it.

Even if you are right about the timing, it would not change what she says today.
Accept, then turn. A concession that ends the sentence gives the point away.

callout.titulo: The objection to expect, and the only answer that works
callout.texto: And what does that buy us? is a fair question, and the answer is never “because it is true”. It is always what it changes about the decision in front of you — which is why the consequence goes in the present: we would not be arguing about it now.
